title: fix: sort dbt debug connection keys alphabetically
body:
Closes #13626

The \debug\ command printed connection details in struct-serialization order, burying key fields like \ccount\ at the bottom of the list. This sorts the filtered connection mapping by key in \	o_connection_mapping()\, so every adapter renders a deterministic, alphabetical order. Secret filtering via \get_connection_keys()\ is unchanged.

Verification:
- Added \	est_connection_mapping_keys_are_sorted_alphabetically\: failed before the fix (order was \client_session_keep_alive, retry_all, ... , account, ...\), passes after (\ccount\ first, \warehouse\ last)
- All 33 \schemas::profiles\ tests pass, including \connection_keys_never_expose_a_credential\
- \cargo clippy -p dbt-schemas --all-targets -- -D warnings\ clean

Note: no changelog entry yet (\changie\ not available in my environment) — happy to add one if required, or a maintainer can apply the \Skip Changelog\ label.

title: Fix nightly PyPI release: pass correct package_name (dbt-core)
body:
## Summary
- The nightly release workflow (`Nightly Test Release to GitHub and PyPI`) has been failing every run at `validate-package-available-pypi`, always with "Manual intervention required" (e.g. runs 35204535784 through 36232307332).
- Root cause: `dbt-labs/dbt-release/.github/workflows/pypi-release.yml` derives the PyPI package name from the calling repo's name via `sanitize-package-name`. This repo is named `dbt`, but the package actually published is `dbt-core`, so the workflow's post-publish verification step checks PyPI/TestPyPI for a package literally named `dbt` — an unrelated package — instead of `dbt-core`. The actual `dbt-core` upload succeeds every time; only the verification is checking the wrong name.
- This PR passes the new `package_name: dbt-core` input (added in dbt-labs/dbt-release#174) so the verification checks the right package.

**Depends on:** https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-release/pull/174 being merged first — this repo calls that reusable workflow at `@main`, and the `package_name` input doesn't exist until that PR lands.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge dbt-labs/dbt-release#174 first.
- [ ] Merge this PR.
- [ ] Confirm the next scheduled nightly run (or a manual `workflow_dispatch`) of "Nightly Test Release to GitHub and PyPI" passes `validate-package-available-pypi`.

title: fix(databricks): stage V1 view replacements of non-view relations
body:
Resolves #16476

Port of databricks/dbt-databricks#1688

### Problem

With `use_materialization_v2` off (the default), when a Databricks view model replaces an existing table or other non-view relation, the view materialization drops the existing relation first and only then creates the view. If the view fails to build, the run fails and the table is already gone.

### Solution

Route that case through `get_replace_sql`, the replacement flow the V2 view path already uses. The view is created at the `__dbt_stg` staging relation first, then swapped in, so a failed build leaves the existing table in place. V1 and V2 now replace a relation of a different type the same way. View-over-view runs keep the existing `create or replace view` path, and grants and tags are applied in the same order as before.

The V1 branch of the vendored `view.sql` matches #1688 byte for byte. The replace-flow macros it calls (`get_replace_sql`, `create_backup`, `execute_multiple_statements`) are already vendored and match current dbt-databricks.

The `dbt-loader` view materialization test for an existing Databricks table now asserts that the first statement creates the view at the staging relation and that the table is renamed out of the way. It fails on `main`, where the view is created directly at the target after the drop.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.
- [ ] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.
- [x] This PR includes tests, or tests are not required or relevant for this PR.
- [x] This PR has no interface changes (e.g., macros, CLI, logs, JSON artifacts, config files, adapter interface, etc.) or this PR has already received feedback and approval from Product or DX.

title: fix(bigquery): resolve seed files from the package root
body:
Resolves #16127.

BigQuery seeds fail when dbt runs outside the project root because the seed macro concatenates a missing `model['project_root']` field with the project-relative `original_file_path`.

Use the existing `adapter.get_seed_file_path(model)` method, which resolves the seed path from its package root.
